page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained vCPU configuration. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It integrates 256.0 GB of memory, resulting in an exceptionally high allocation of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. Bundled hardware features include 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2,051.0 and solid text processing throughput. Multi-core performance metrics, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,780.0 and PassMark CPU score of 14,316.24, remain in the middle tier, bounded by the 8 vCPU cap. The system demonstrates robust uncached memory throughput with large block read speeds reaching 66.17 GB/sec and write speeds of 45.13 GB/sec. In-memory data workloads such as Redis reach 11.06 million SET operations per second, though synthetic PassMark memory testing lands in the lower quartile.

The constrained vCPU allocation offers a specific architectural tradeoff: it provides the total memory footprint and local NVMe storage of a 32-core class system while constraining core count to 8 vCPUs. This configuration significantly reduces per-core software licensing overhead without forfeiting the massive 256.0 GB memory capacity. Workload profiles that benefit most include memory-intensive enterprise relational databases, caching layers, high-density in-memory analytics, and software deployments restricted by core-based software licensing.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers an expansive 256.0 GB of memory—providing 32.0 GB per vCPU—and includes 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core capabilities, registering 2,051.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, alongside 11.06 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Multi-threaded compute capacity is capped by the 8 vCPU limit, reflecting an intentional architecture designed for memory-heavy and high-storage workloads that must control per-core licensing expenses. Consequently, the E32-8ds_v6 is well suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing.
